Elena/Ben —

Thanks for bringing this up. For context, Redwood’s legal position on remedies beyond credits: we prefer structured cure/mitigation plans and capped financial exposure rather than open-ended liquidated damages. That said, we can consider a limited fee-at-risk and a staged termination right with the following guardrails:

- Cure ladder: 30 days to investigate/remediate first P1; 30-day cure after second P1; final termination allowed only after three verified P1 incidents within a rolling 120-day window and failure to remedy within 30 days after notice.
- Fee-at-risk: an escrowed holdback up to 12% of committed monthly spend, released pro rata once remediation steps are completed. The escrow can step down after each 60-day stability window.
- Liability: liability remains subject to our existing caps and exclusions (force majeure, third-party infra providers).
- Measurement: incidents must be validated against agreed observability signals (endpoint latency metrics, error rates) and mutually agreed post-incident review.

I’m attaching a redline that reflects the above — it’s intentionally conservative. If Medixa needs a liquidated damages table tied to measurable business outcomes, that will need exec sign-off and a tailored damages formula.

If Ben can confirm Medixa’s required thresholds and any internal procurement deadlines, I’ll prioritize a redline iteration.

Regards,
